description: Demo Labs at DEF CON Safe Mode showcases open-source security tools, vulnerability scanners, and testing frameworks demonstrated by their creators.

talks.title: Safe Mode Demo Labs - Jakub Botwicz
talks.teaser: A live demonstration of Cotopaxi, an open-source testing framework for evaluating Internet of Things device protocol security.
talks.summary:
Security researcher and Samsung R&D penetration tester Jakub Botwicz demonstrates Cotopaxi, an open-source security assessment toolkit designed to evaluate the protocol security of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in the Demo Labs [00:01, 00:08].

Botwicz explores how the toolkit automates vulnerability discovery, protocol fuzzing, and security testing across specialized IoT protocols including CoAP, DTLS, and mDNS [00:43, 14:38]. He demonstrates testing amplification vulnerabilities in network services—identifying an amplification factor of up to 2048x on vulnerable endpoints [22:05]—and shows how developers can integrate Cotopaxi into CI/CD pipelines to harden IoT network stacks [28:45].

talks.title: Safe Mode Demo Labs - Vincent Rose
talks.teaser: A walkthrough of Starkiller, a graphical user interface frontend for managing PowerShell Empire post-exploitation agents and operations.
talks.summary:
In this technical demonstration from DEF CON Safe Mode Demo Labs, core developers Anthony (Coin), Jake (Hubble), and Vincent Rose showcase Starkiller, the multi-user graphical user interface for PowerShell Empire. Opening at 00:06, the team explains how they forked and modernized the post-exploitation framework following the sunset of the original project, expanding it to over 300 active modules.

At 02:00 and 04:00, the presenters demonstrate the Starkiller interface, showing how red team operators connect to a centralized Empire team server, manage active listeners, and task compromised endpoints collaboratively.

At 10:00 and 15:01, the demo highlights filtering post-exploitation modules by MITRE ATT&CK tactics, executing stealthy lateral movement commands, and generating dynamic stagers to emulate advanced adversary tradecraft during enterprise security assessments. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Safe Mode Demo Labs - Tamoaki Tani - malconfscan with cuckoo
talks.teaser: A demonstration of using MalConfScan with Cuckoo Sandbox to extract configuration data from malware families in memory.
talks.summary:
Researchers Tomoaki Tani and Shusei Tomonaga from JPCERT/CC demonstrate "MalConfScan with Cuckoo," an automated memory forensic plugin for Cuckoo Sandbox that automatically extracts configuration data and command-and-control (C2) infrastructure from infected Windows and Linux hosts [00:04, 03:42].

The presenters demonstrate live extraction workflows on real-world malware families, such as the TSCookie backdoor used by BlackTech and Ursnif banking malware [07:49, 11:55]. They explain how the tool leverages Volatility memory analysis to bypass sophisticated anti-analysis techniques—such as VM detection checks searching for "VBox" or "VMware" device names [15:05]—allowing incident responders to extract decrypted C2 IP addresses, domains, and operational configurations in seconds [19:15].

talks.title: Safe Mode Demo Labs - Ajin Abraham - Mobile App Security Testing with MobSF
talks.teaser: A demonstration of Mobile Security Framework (MobSF) for performing automated static and dynamic security analysis of mobile apps.
talks.summary:
In this hands-on tool demonstration from DEF CON Safe Mode Demo Labs, security researcher and project creator Ajin Abraham presents Mobile Security Framework (MobSF), an open-source automated security assessment platform for Android and iOS applications. Opening at 00:00, Ajin introduces MobSF's dual capabilities in static and dynamic analysis.

At 07:00, he demonstrates static binary analysis, showing how MobSF parses application manifests, decompiles binaries, identifies hardcoded secrets, and maps exported components and permissions to pinpoint attack surfaces.

Moving to dynamic testing at 14:00 and 21:00, Ajin executes applications on an instrumented emulator, demonstrating real-time API hooking via Frida scripts to bypass certificate pinning, intercept encrypted HTTPS traffic using MobSF's root CA, and inspect local SQLite databases at 28:00 for leaked sensitive data. talks.title: CIRCO v2: Stealth Hardware Implant for Network Credential Harvesting
talks.teaser: Emilio Couto demonstrates CIRCO v2, a stealthy Raspberry Pi hardware implant camouflaged inside a PoE injector that tricks enterprise network automation systems into exposing credentials.
talks.summary:
Camouflaged Physical Network Implants

Physical red team engagements frequently require covert implants capable of evading discovery by facility staff and security controls while remaining connected to target networks.

Hardware Architecture of CIRCO v2

Emilio Couto presents CIRCO v2, an offensive platform built on a Raspberry Pi form factor and housed within a nondescript PoE injector or surface-mount network outlet box.

Stealth Telemetry and Anti-Tamper Controls

The device incorporates hardware sensors—including ambient light detectors to trigger self-erasure or alert ops upon enclosure opening—and MAC/IP spoofing to evade 802.1X and NAC monitoring.

Autonomous Credential Harvesting and Exfiltration

Couto demonstrates CIRCO's automated decoy services and honeypots that bait IT management systems into authenticating, capturing plaintext credentials via Net-Creds and exfiltrating data covertly.
